author: sonnet
label: pilot-01
changes: Moved the lapsed-hold policy into a Decisions section as a single claim rule (HELD, EXPIRED with retake, RELEASED) and stated that the 10-minute hold does not guarantee stock at payment time; simplified the claim node label.

Defined which order states count as no longer waiting for a late PaymentSucceeded, and what happens if success arrives after a decline (refund, order stays cancelled; CONFIRMED duplicates ignored; Payment alerts on contradictory outcomes).

Stated why Order uses HTTP for Cart and Inventory and events for Payment, and added a 'When a call fails' section covering reserve timeout, lost claim response, Cart unreachable, and charge retry; added CANCELLED_SYSTEM_ERROR.
Added a Customer node and the AWAITING_PAYMENT message (order received, confirming payment, live status page), explained PENDING as transient, and added the confirmation email.
Decided that retry after a decline creates a new order with a new id and charge key, and that only PENDING or AWAITING_PAYMENT orders are returned on a repeated press.

Gave refund retry a clear owner: Payment's retry worker reads next_attempt_at from the refunds row, ops 'Retry now' is an admin endpoint that resets it, and exhausting attempts alerts and slows retries but never ends them.
Tracked refunds on the order with refund_status (REFUND_PENDING, REFUNDED), set on RefundCompleted with a customer email, and removed the unfinished-ending assumption.

Cut the triggers table, the failure branches table and the 'Why the claim step exists' section; moved behaviour-changing assumptions (lapsed hold, cart emptying) into Decisions and left only genuinely open items in 'To confirm'.
Added a short happy-path diagram first and split the large flowchart into a checkout/outcome diagram and a separate refund diagram, keeping each service's stored data in its subgraph title.

Point 1: Decision 1 now defines release for every reservation status. Release on EXPIRED sets RELEASED with no stock change, so a decline after the hold lapsed is clean and a later claim is refused. Release is also shown in the Phase 3 diagram.
Point 2: The PaymentSucceeded decision node in Phase 2 now has three branches (AWAITING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED ignored, any other status refunded). Decision 3 lists exactly which statuses get a refund.

Point 3: Decision 4 now says refund_status can be set on any non-CONFIRMED order that took money, including CANCELLED_PAYMENT_DECLINED and CANCELLED_SYSTEM_ERROR. It also notes these are a safety net, since Payment is only asked to charge AWAITING_PAYMENT orders.
Point 4: Replaced the nested state list with a transition table. Every transition shows its source state and trigger, including those from PENDING. Final states are named.

Point 5: Decision 2 now defines 'this cart' as the cart id. It names a partial unique index on orders(cart_id) for PENDING and AWAITING_PAYMENT, and explains how a concurrent press loses and returns the existing order. It adds a 2-minute sweeper for stuck PENDING orders. The diagram shows the index check.

Point 6: Added the claim sweeper to the Phase 3 diagram. After 15 minutes without an answer, the page shows a delay message, the customer gets one email, and ops is alerted then hourly. It keeps resending and never refunds without an answer, and the reason is stated. A manual-override question moved to To confirm.

Point 7: Added a Keys and constraints table defining every key exactly. The claim key is claim: + order id, and the refund key is refund: + order id. Decision 1 makes claim idempotent by storing its outcome on the reservation, so a retry of an EXPIRED re-take returns the same result and changes no stock.

Point 8: Decision 5 now removes only the snapshotted lines on OrderConfirmed, by reducing quantity, and keeps items added later. Cart dedupes on order id in processed_events. The 'Cart edits' open question is removed.

Point 8: Split the one large diagram into four phase diagrams (reserve, payment outcome, claim and release, refund) under the happy-path overview. Customer messages are folded into the steps that send them instead of a separate Customer swimlane.
Updated 'How to read this' to explain the split, and the overview diagram's last step to say only snapshotted lines are removed.
Phase 1 diagram: merged the two duplicate O2 to I1 edges into one labelled edge ('no, new order. HTTP reserve, key = order id').

Phase 1 diagram: made the order explicit as fetch from Cart, build snapshot (new node O2S), then insert and unique-index check; added an empty-cart branch (nothing saved, customer told) and added new Decision 3 stating the snapshot uses the lines and prices Cart returned and the customer is charged the snapshot total.

Decision 1: replaced 'can never all win' with plain wording that expiry, claim and release are serialised and the first to run decides; stated that the up-to-one-minute hold overrun is acceptable and that a claim on a still-HELD past-expiry reservation succeeds.
How to read this: added an up-front bullet that a paid order can still end as out of stock, by design, and why.

Order states: added a Refund column and rows for PaymentSucceeded repeat on CONFIRMED and late PaymentSucceeded on CANCELLED_*; clarified that REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK and PENDING system-error cancellations never have a refund because payment is never requested; replaced the misleading 'except' sentence with 'any event not listed is ignored'; added the refund_status progression.

Decision 4 (was 3): removed the unreachable PENDING and REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK refund cases; rule is now AWAITING_PAYMENT starts claim, CONFIRMED ignored, any other status refunded. Explained why a refund cannot race an in-flight claim.
Merged the repeated refund-state lists of old Decisions 3 and 4 into one rule plus a single table, shortening Decision 5 (refund tracking).

Added Decision 7 and Phase 3 text on Order crashing after a granted claim: the order stays AWAITING_PAYMENT and the sweeper resends the same claim key, which returns CLAIMED. Noted the manual-override gap remains in To confirm.

Stated where the paid flag lives: Order stores payment_succeeded_at when handling PaymentSucceeded, in the same transaction as claim_started_at and the outbox row; sweeper and Phase 2/3 diagrams now use it.

Clarified refund ownership: Payment executes refunds, Order's refund_status is set in the same transaction as the RefundRequested outbox row, so a lost message is republished by the relay; added this to Phase 4.
Marked all retry and timeout numbers as initial configuration values in 'How to read this' and 'To confirm' so the body no longer reads as fixed.

Phase 3 diagram: split the dense sweeper alert node into three nodes (order page message, one customer email, ops alert); Phase 1 timer node now notes the up-to-one-minute overrun; Phase 2 diagram wording aligned with the new refund rule.
